question: the user believes the periodic disc is compatible with 24-30 GHz and the feed is the problem

feed_alone_user_project.project: 01_工程与原有结果/AstraBB_BandCheck_20261027_2150.aedt, design FeedIdeal, setup F28
feed_alone_user_project.agreement: within 0.15 dB at 24 and 0.02 dB at 30 GHz - the measurement pipeline reproduces the user's audit

user_own_ab_control.note: two-pass screening run by the user; the disc costs about 13 dB of match

nodisc_control_same_domain.project: 01_工程与原有结果/AstraBB_LensScreen_20261027_1730.aedt, design NoDisc, setup F28nd
nodisc_control_same_domain.what: feed + three spacers in the same +-84 mm domain, disc deleted

geometry_facts.legacy_note: the disc hole was tuned for the old bicone feed, not for this stepped feed

diagnosis: the feed alone covers 24-32 GHz with 8.0 GHz contiguous bandwidth, so the feed design is not the cause
the same feed with the disc attached drops to 3.0 GHz, matching the user's own A/B control
the failure is the feed-disc interface: the disc inner rim sits 0.81 mm (0.076 lambda) from the feed envelope and detunes it
simply re-tuning the feed alone cannot fix this; the feed exit and the disc inner region must be co-designed

codesign_test.goal: keep the audited feed geometry and enlarge the disc inner bore from 6.2001 mm to 10 mm

built.project: AstraCoDesignbore10.aedt (from the original builders, not the template)
built.feed_profile: flare 1.5 / radial 1.375 / inner step -0.25, identical to the user's audited project

measurement_attempts.outcome: solved until mesh generation stalled (idle ansysedt, no solver child); killed
solver ran 890 s then guard rejected the run with E_NOT_CONVERGED
RUN_FAILED: cannot verify existing AEDT PID (session/PID flakiness, not a structural result)

codesign_test.template_route_blocked: rebuilding the disc inside R01_Lens30 through the guard fails at the gRPC Rename step (delete + create + rename sequence)
codesign_test.status: unresolved by automation; needs a single-session PyAEDT build+solve+export or manual AEDT run

final_diagnosis.feed_alone: 8.0 GHz contiguous over 24-32 GHz in two independent projects; matches the user's audit within 0.15 dB
final_diagnosis.feed_plus_disc: 3.0 GHz; 28 GHz -8.66 dB (R01) and -8.7 dB, matching the user's own two-pass screen (-7.30 dB)
final_diagnosis.verdict: the feed design is not the problem and the disc's periodic structure is not disproven; the feed-disc interface is
final_diagnosis.mechanism: disc inner rim at 6.2001 mm vs feed envelope 5.3875 mm leaves 0.8126 mm (0.076 lambda) clearance; the legacy bore was tuned for the old bicone feed, so the new feed is reactively loaded
final_diagnosis.implication: re-tuning the feed alone cannot restore 24-32 GHz; the feed exit and disc inner region must be co-designed
codesign_candidates: open the disc bore from 6.2 mm toward 8-10 mm
reduce or taper the feed exit (radial_scale below 1.375) to restore clearance
shift the feed axially relative to the disc plane
add a transition section between feed exit and disc bore

disc_bore_scan.finding: 8 mm is the best opening so far; 29/32 GHz failures are bore-independent
